content:
Made event name input more robust by capliatlising event names while compensating for acronyms.
Placed limits on the date of events to between 8 years in the past and 7 days in the future. This prevents incorrect user date input when tryping the date of an event.

Added some input strngthening when adding a new cadet so that inputs are automatically trimmed and capitalised.
Enabled compatibility for multi-name forenames and hyphenated names.
Enabled ability to edit cadet details. If a cadet's name is changes, all events under that name have the name field changed so names changes are pushed to all dashboards.
Added a Change Log to decribe and log releases to the user. Versions in the change log used to inform the version number in the bottom right of the app.

Users can now add badges by clicking on empty cells in the PTS Tracker. Currently a bug exists where a badge added on the PTS Tracker, they must refresh the tracker before remvoing the event from the Mass Event Log. The Badge displays correctly in the Mass Event Log, the End of Year Certificate and counts towards Flight Points.
Made changelog show versions in correct order (where v0.10.x shows after v0.9.x).
Fixed bug where the setEvent function (used to add badges via the PTS Tracker) did not properly save events to data context meaning they had could not be deleted without refreshing the page.

Made mass event log use same function as PTS Tracker to add event.
Refactored save event function to a react hook to make it easier to use in multiple components.
Added duplicate event/badge/exam protection by showing a warning in the console when the user attempts to add a duplicate record. Warning does not show as popup or alert for a smoother user experience.

Users can now add classification records/exams to a cadet's record directly using the Classification Tracker by clicking on a cadet (graph scatter point or table row) and adding 1 or more exams/records. These additions are saved to the database and are reflected in the Mass Event Log, End of Year Certificate and Flight Points dashboard.
Edited database formatting to enable Firestore rules. This included changes to database structure and the specific collections written to when new and existing users access the tracker.
Fixed bug where adding events to PTS Tracker when the badge category had two words (i.e. First Aid) would only save as the first part of the badge category (i.e. Blue First).
Updated list of acronyms for record auto-formatting to include 'MOI'.

Added a new feature to the PTS Tracker that allows users to filter by time range or show all. Also added totals row to each column. This will make it easier to get PTS insights and for reporting during administrative inspections.
Fixed highlighting best cadets in Flight Points Dashboard. Also Fixed sorting flights as numbers rather than strings. Also fixed the displayed version on the app.
Allowed adding flight points to a flight in the context of flight competitions.

Groundwork for the flights work below, with no change to how anything is used. An automated test suite now runs on every change, Firestore security rules restrict each squadron to its own data, and the app has moved to a faster build.
Pop-up alerts have been replaced with messages shown inside the app, so a warning no longer blocks the page until it is dismissed.

A squadron is no longer fixed at three flights. A new Flights screen (admin only) lets you add flights, rename them, choose which ones compete for points, and archive ones no longer in use. The Flight Points dashboard, the flight picker when adding a cadet, and the new-squadron setup form all follow whatever the squadron has configured.
There is deliberately no delete. Archiving retires a flight and removes it from the picker and the points chart, while its cadets and their history stay intact. A flight that still holds cadets cannot be archived.
At least one flight must be competing, and flight names must be unique. Existing squadrons keep working unchanged until an admin edits their flights.

The Admin Area can now download a backup of the squadron as a zip of four CSV files: cadets, the event log, flight points and squadron information. Discharging a cadet permanently deletes their record, so take a backup before doing so.
Web app account information (emails, access requests and permissions) is deliberately excluded, so the file can be shared without sharing anyone's account details.

Dark mode. Use the sun/moon button in the header to switch; your choice is saved to your account, so it follows you to any device you sign in on. If you have never chosen, the app follows whatever your device is set to.
Behind the scenes this is a large tidy-up of how the app is styled. Every colour now has a name in one place, which is what made a second theme possible at all. Along the way a number of long-standing oddities were fixed: popups could appear at different sizes depending on which screens you had visited first, the success message was unstyled unless you had opened the Cadet List, and dropdowns looked different from page to page for the same reason.
Popups are now proper dialogs -- they trap focus, close on Escape, and announce themselves to screen readers, none of which they did before. Charts follow the theme, and no longer animate, which respects the reduced-motion setting.

Fixes to dark mode: the access request cards, the PTS Tracker buttons and totals, the certificate panels and the Flight Points table were all hard to read.
Allocating points to a flight now works. Points were being saved and then discarded again straight away, so nothing ever appeared on the chart. If you tried this and thought you had done something wrong, you had not.
Every popup is now the same shape, with Cancel and the confirming button always in the same places, and the menu collapse tab no longer shows through them. Buttons are a little deeper in colour so the white text on them is properly readable.
